evidence: Cic. Sen. 26: senectūs … sit operōsa et semper agēns aliquid
terms.comment: The ordinary word, and also old people as a group, as in senectūs semper agēns aliquid. Its opposite is adulēscentia.

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov.; in ōrātiōne solūtā post Augustum

phrases.latin: senectūs nōn modo languida atque iners nōn sit, vērum etiam sit operōsa et semper agēns aliquid et mōliēns
phrases.english: old age is not sluggish or idle, but busy, always doing and building something

phrases.latin: senectūs autem aetātis est perāctiō tamquam fābulae
phrases.english: old age is the last act of life, as of a play
Old age is itself a disease.

phrases.latin: lēnior et melior fīs accēdente senectā?
phrases.english: are you growing gentler and better as old age comes on?
